outcomes.text: Frame open-ended problems, select AI tools, evaluate outputs, coordinate AI agents and communicate results. Build a portfolio demonstrating responsible professional AI use.

courses.name: Data in the Age of AI
courses.description: Fall 2026 public course listing: Introduces major AI approaches and evaluates which questions they can answer, emphasizing data quality, generative-tool risks, transparent analysis and complementary model behavior.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CSCI 140, 141, minimum score of 1 in 'CSCI 141 Equivalent', DATA 141, 101 or AAI 101. A minimum grade of D- is required in CSCI 140, CSCI 141, DATA 141, DATA 101 and AAI 101. Enrollment is limited to International Honours, Undergraduate or VCCS/RB Co-Enroll Articulation level students.

category_review.locator: Fall2026 public PATH course-detail panel; exact code/section/description/registration restrictions
category_review.rationale: The actual description centers on AI approaches, modeling frameworks, appropriate strategy selection and failure modes, rather than generic programming or an inferred subject from the DATA prefix.

courses.name: AI & Data Ethics
courses.description: Fall 2026 public course listing: Examines ethical, legal, historical and social issues in data and AI, including privacy, discrimination, transparency, responsibility, research practice and system deployment.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment is limited to International Honours, Undergraduate or VCCS/RB Co-Enroll Articulation level students.

category_review.locator: Fall2026 public PATH course-detail panel; exact code/section/description/registration restrictions
category_review.rationale: The full course description centers ethical and social analysis of AI/data systems; it does not become technical AI merely because AI is its object.

courses.name: Designing AI Agents
courses.description: Fall 2026 public course listing: Designs and evaluates agentic generative-AI workflows using prompt pipelines, retrieval augmentation, multi-agent methods and function-calling tools, with attention to reliability and ethical limits.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisite: DATA 201. A minimum grade of D- is required in DATA 201. Enrollment is limited to International Honours, Undergraduate or VCCS/RB Co-Enroll Articulation level students.

category_review.locator: Fall2026 public PATH course-detail panel; exact code/section/description/registration restrictions
category_review.rationale: The actual description explicitly teaches construction and evaluation of generative-AI agent workflows and tools. Its technical AI subject is now supported by content, not the short title alone.

requirements.title: Major credit minimum
requirements.summary: The department describes a 30-credit undergraduate major. This is the major total, not the complete BA degree total.

requirements.title: Core courses named in residency policy
requirements.summary: The FAQ explicitly names these core courses. This is an incomplete inventory; DATA 305 conflicts with AAI 301 in the linked example pathway.

requirements.title: Transfer, AP and cross-department substitutions
requirements.summary: Substitutions require departmental review of the prior course and syllabus; curriculum committee approval may be required.

requirements.title: External-faculty independent research
requirements.summary: For DATA 490 with a faculty member outside Data Science, the faculty member submits a proposal of no more than one page describing goals, data, methods and the desired 3 or 4 credits. Curriculum committee approval is required.

requirements.title: Study abroad and residency
requirements.summary: Study-abroad credit requires departmental preapproval. The listed core courses should be taken at W&M, with rare exceptions requiring curriculum committee consent; the capstone must be completed at W&M.

requirements.title: Study-abroad equivalency
requirements.summary: Equivalent approved courses transfer under the corresponding W&M course number after faculty review. Relevant courses without a W&M equivalent may transfer as DATA 340 after faculty and curriculum committee review.

requirements.title: Arts & Sciences declaration
requirements.summary: Students already in Arts & Sciences may declare directly without a separate application to the School of Computing, Data Sciences & Physics.

requirements.title: Major declaration and advising
requirements.summary: Declare after 39–54 earned credit hours, including AP, IB and transfer credit. Request an advisor, review the major declaration with the advisor, and submit the signed form to the Registrar. Annual advisor check-ins are recommended.

requirements.title: Earned-credit declaration thresholds
requirements.summary: Major declaration is permitted at 39 earned credits and required at 54; in-progress credits do not count. Entrants with AP, IB or dual-enrollment credit may wait until 39 credits earned since high school; transfers entering with at least 54 credits may wait until the end of their first W&M semester.

requirements.title: Major declaration review and changes
requirements.summary: Use a What If degree audit and major worksheet; the student and major advisor must sign. Double majors submit separate forms. Major changes must be submitted before the last add/drop day of the final semester. Program-specific declaration instructions continue to apply.

requirements.title: Major, minor and degree relationship
requirements.summary: The form explicitly includes the School of Computing, Data Sciences and Physics: one major is required; students may have two majors or one major and a minor. W&M awards one baccalaureate degree based on the primary major; two majors do not constitute two degrees.

requirements.title: Elective pass/fail eligibility
requirements.summary: Actively enrolled bachelor’s-degree students who are social juniors or seniors may elect pass/fail for up to four standard-grade undergraduate electives in the listed schools, explicitly including CDSP. At most two may come from one semester and at most two may be retroactive. Elections are irrevocable; changing an already graded course requires advisor or chair consultation and the applicable published deadline.

requirements.title: Pass/fail exclusions and GPA
requirements.summary: COLL, arts/math/language proficiency and major/minor requirements cannot be elected pass/fail unless the course is inherently pass/fail only. A course with an Honor Code grade consequence is ineligible. P does not affect GPA; F does. Pass/fail credit counts toward the 12-credit enrollment minimum but not the Dean’s List graded-credit minimum. An exception request does not grant approval; BUAD elections have their own school petition route.

requirements.title: Post-matriculation outside-credit approval
requirements.summary: Outside work after matriculation requires advance approval and academic good standing. It transfers as elective credit unless additional prior approval permits major, minor or proficiency use. This general procedure does not waive the Applied AI core/capstone residence requirements.

requirements.title: Domestic study-away timing and load
requirements.summary: Domestic full-time study-away approval is due before the previous term ends. Summer outside-study permission must be approved before spring classes end. Fall/spring students ordinarily enroll in at least 12 W&M credits; taking work elsewhere instead requires withdrawal, prior permission, relevant departmental/committee approvals and readmission before credit posts. Winter outside study permits up to four credits, requested by December 1 and approved before fall classes end.

requirements.title: Repeat policy effective Fall 2025
requirements.summary: Under the policy effective Fall 2025, a non-repeatable course with earned C− or higher cannot be repeated for credit. D-range or failed courses may be repeated; only the latest attempt supplies credit/GPA, while both grades remain visible. Once a repeat earns credit no further repeat is allowed, but the published examples permit successive failures and reengagement after losing prior D credit to an F. The generic one-repeat sentence is interpreted alongside these explicit examples, not as an unconditional two-attempt cap.

requirements.title: Repeat identity and transfer restrictions
requirements.summary: A course already credited through transfer cannot be repeated; an already credited W&M course cannot later be transferred in, even after a D-range grade. Outside repeats do not replace W&M GPA. Rotating topics are distinct for this policy; repeating a variable-credit course requires the same credit amount. A repeat does not retroactively change the original term’s academic standing. No course-equivalence identity is inferred from these restrictions.

requirements.title: University-wide academic exception process
requirements.summary: The Committee on Academic Exceptions now handles undergraduate exceptions across schools, replacing the former degree/status committees. Approval is not automatic and ordinarily requires extraordinary circumstances, a supporting professor statement and a written decision. Students continue their current schedule until notified; a denied petition may be appealed within five business days with new information. A procedure is not a granted substitution or waiver.

requirements.title: Conditional underload and overload
requirements.summary: A final-term student who has applied to graduate and is enrolled in all remaining degree courses may seek fewer than 12 credits through the Registrar; other underloads require the relevant accommodation or committee route. Registrar review of a 19-credit overload requires a continuing degree student, no incompletes, good standing and GPA at least 3.00. Other cases or loads above 19 require committee review. Summer registration permits up to 16 credits; larger loads require a petition. None of these conditions creates a new degree-credit total.

requirements.title: Conditional study-abroad eligibility and load
requirements.summary: Study abroad requires active good standing and eligibility to study at Williamsburg; the page specifies reinstatement/approval routes for students with adverse status rather than an automatic waiver. Semester/year programs normally require 12–18 W&M credits; an approved underload/overload must precede the program. Non-W&M programs before an on-campus semester must finish at least two days before that semester starts. Summer aid requires at least six W&M credits; winter has no published minimum on this page.

requirements.title: Study-abroad credit, grades and approval
requirements.summary: Non-W&M transfer study requires faculty approval, an official host transcript and at least C; it does not carry W&M GPA or allow pass/fail. W&M faculty-led/embedded courses and specified Seville/La Plata courses carry grades and credit; the only stated abroad pass/fail exception is the two named semester programs under the normal policy. At least 60 degree credits must come from W&M. Transfer approvals must be completed during the following semester, including at least 12 credits per semester abroad and all summer/winter credits. Major/minor use requires prior departmental approval and remains subject to Applied AI’s own residence restrictions.

requirements.title: Study-abroad COLL allocation
requirements.summary: Registered global education may satisfy COLL300 after successful credit transfer, C-or-better grades, course approvals and the required reflection. Other COLL/attributes are unavailable except pre-assigned W&M faculty-led/embedded attributes or an approved petition. COLL300 eligibility is not automatic permission to satisfy other distributions.

requirements.title: Study-abroad internship and independent work
requirements.summary: Full-time internships require advance approval and an academic assignment/project for any credit; internship activity alone does not earn credit. Independent-study arrangements require advance faculty consultation and W&M credit is awarded in the term after return because simultaneous credit with the external program would be prohibited dual enrollment.

requirements.title: Graduation application and certification
requirements.summary: Graduation candidates must check their degree audit and holds and submit the graduation application by the published cohort deadline. Late filing may affect award of the degree and must be discussed with the undergraduate graduation coordinator. The public application procedure does not itself certify completion of the full BA curriculum.

requirements.title: COLL applies across undergraduate schools
requirements.summary: The public overview expressly applies COLL to all W&M undergraduates, including this CDSP-hosted BA. AP/IB may support domain electives and proficiencies but do not replace the named COLL sequence. Specific transfer exceptions are mapped separately.

requirements.title: First-year COLL requirements
requirements.summary: Complete one designated COLL100 and one COLL150 in the first year, each at C− or better, subject to the explicit incoming-transfer exceptions. These are designation criteria, not individual course identities.

requirements.title: COLL200 and separate domain electives
requirements.summary: Complete three knowledge-domain electives, at least three credits each in ALV, CSI and NQR. Separately, COLL200 requires nine credits with at least three in each domain. The same course cannot satisfy both a required COLL allocation and a domain elective; transfer exceptions may alter the applicable selection.

requirements.title: Upper COLL designation requirements
requirements.summary: Complete at least one designated course totaling three credits for COLL300, similarly three credits for COLL350, and one COLL400 course of at least three credits. These open attribute criteria do not claim an exhaustive finite course pool or automatically equate the major capstone with COLL400.

requirements.title: Foreign-language proficiency alternatives
requirements.summary: Demonstrate natural-language proficiency other than English at level 202/IV through four high-school years in one language, qualifying AP/IB/transfer credit, a college 202-or-higher course, or an approved native-language exemption petition. Satisfying an alternative removes the general additional-language-course obligation; no student exemption is assumed.

requirements.title: Mathematics, arts and overlap criteria
requirements.summary: Mathematics proficiency accepts pre-matriculation calculus/statistics credit or a W&M MATH-attribute course. Creative/performing arts uses the Arts Proficiency attribute. A single course may satisfy a proficiency and COLL requirement, but cannot fill both a required COLL and a knowledge-domain elective. No extra fixed course is inferred when an approved proficiency alternative is met.

requirements.title: Creative and performing arts minimum
requirements.summary: Creative/performing-arts proficiency requires at least two credits of instruction in an eligible art. Eligibility is the published attribute, not every course mentioning music, theatre or art.

requirements.title: Published undergraduate total and pre-matriculation credit
requirements.summary: The public overview states 120 credits to graduate and permits qualifying AP/IB toward that total, domain electives, proficiencies and some major requirements. It points to the catalog for detailed ten-semester and credit-residence rules; those detailed conditions are not invented from this summary.

requirements.title: General incoming-transfer COLL conditions
requirements.summary: The general transfer rules waive COLL100 after at least two full-time post-high-school semesters for entering social sophomores/juniors, require COLL150 at W&M, and place COLL350/400 after matriculation. A prior significant study-abroad/away experience may qualify for COLL300 by application with at least three transferable credits graded C/2.0 or better, transcript and syllabus. Specific tabulated pathways provide additional COLL200/domain exceptions.

requirements.title: Source-specific incoming-transfer exceptions
requirements.summary: The published tables waive mathematics proficiency and all three domain-elective allocations for VCCS Passport, VCCS Uniform Certificate and the listed post-high-school VCCS/RBC associate-degree groups. Passport retains all three COLL200 courses. Uniform Certificate with two post-high-school full-time semesters and the listed associate-degree holders retain one in-residence COLL200 in any domain. Other transfers with at least two such semesters retain two in-residence COLL200 courses in any domain and receive the domain-elective waivers, but no automatic math waiver. COLL150 remains at W&M; COLL350/400 follow matriculation; language/arts still need qualifying evidence. No pathway is assigned without its actual admission credential.

requirements.title: Transfer standing and proficiency scope
requirements.summary: The source, effective Fall 2015 and amended Spring 2022, grants eligible VCCS/RBC university-parallel associate holders junior standing with at least 54 credits through evaluation and if needed academic electives. Applicable transfer/test credits can support proficiencies and domains, but cannot replace COLL150/200/350/400 outside the explicit tabulated waivers. These source policy dates are not this program’s start date. Table language shorthand says three or four high-school years while the general planning guide specifies four; exact student language applicability still needs authoritative clarification.
